name: Swift
summary: Learn Swift bindings, optionals, collections, value semantics, and typed error handling through command-line examples.

prerequisites: Know how to save a plain text file.
Install a Swift 6 toolchain to run examples from a terminal with swift lesson.swift. Reading and exercises work offline.
metadata.miniProject: Build a pantry inventory tool. Parse counts without force-unwrapping, store items and quantities in a dictionary, and report invalid entries with a specific error. Print items in sorted order so output stays predictable.

references.title: The Swift Programming Language: The Basics
The Swift Programming Language: Collection Types
The Swift Programming Language: Error Handling

lessons.title: Bindings, types, and interpolation
lessons.explanation: Use let for a binding that keeps its value and var for one you plan to change. Swift infers types from many initializers. String interpolation puts a value into text.
lessons.example:
let item: String = "notebook"
let centsPerItem = 225
var quantity = 2
quantity += 1
print("\(quantity) \(item)s cost \(quantity * centsPerItem) cents")

api.name: \(expression)
api.description: Insert the value of an expression into a string literal.

lessons.practice: Start with four notebooks, then add two. Print the final count and price in cents.
lessons.pitfall: Swift does not implicitly add an Int and a Double. Choose one numeric type or convert deliberately.

references.title: The Swift Programming Language: The Basics

exercise.expected: Report the final quantity and total price with string interpolation.
exercise.completion: Six notebooks cost 1350 cents. Changing the price changes the total.

lessons.title: Optionals and guard clauses
lessons.explanation: An optional represents either a value or its absence. Int(text) returns an optional because conversion can fail. A guard unwraps valid values for the rest of the function and its else block leaves that scope.

api.name: String?
api.description: Represent a string that may be absent.

api.name: guard let
api.description: Bind an optional value when the required condition holds.

api.name: Int(text)
api.description: Try to convert a string into an integer.

lessons.practice: Require a count from two to eight and return two when input is missing or invalid.
lessons.pitfall: Force-unwrapping with ! traps at runtime if the optional is nil. Choose a fallback or handle the missing case.

references.title: The Swift Programming Language: The Basics
The Swift Programming Language: Control Flow

exercise.expected: Accept a valid count and use a fallback for empty, malformed, or out-of-range values.
exercise.completion: The inputs "5", "10", and nil produce 5, 2, and 2.

lessons.title: Arrays and dictionaries
lessons.explanation: An array keeps an ordered sequence. A dictionary stores values by key. A dictionary lookup is optional when the key may be absent. A defaulted subscript supplies a starting value for a count.

api.name: Dictionary
api.description: Look up a value by key.

api.name: dictionary[key, default: value]
api.description: Provide a default when reading or updating a missing key.

lessons.practice: Count tokens in a short list of fruits. Sort the result by fruit name.
lessons.pitfall: Dictionary iteration has no promised sorted order. Sort keys when the output has to be stable.

references.title: The Swift Programming Language: Collection Types

exercise.expected: Print each distinct fruit once with the number of times it appears.
exercise.completion: The list ["pear", "apple", "pear"] prints apple with count 1 before pear with count 2.

lessons.title: Structs and value semantics
lessons.explanation: A struct groups related values. Assigning an ordinary struct copies its value, so the two bindings can change independently. A mutating method can change the stored properties of a struct.

api.name: struct
api.description: Define a value type with properties and methods.

api.name: mutating
api.description: Allow a method to modify the struct value.

api.name: Basket(items:)
api.description: Initialize the stored property of a simple struct.

lessons.practice: Write a Timer struct that adds seconds and reports the resulting count. Test a copy of a timer.
lessons.pitfall: A let-bound struct cannot be mutated through that binding. If a struct stores a reference, copying it can still share the referenced object.

references.title: The Swift Programming Language: Structures and Classes

exercise.expected: Increment one timer while a copied value keeps its original count.
exercise.completion: Starting at 10 and adding 5 to the copy prints 10 and 15.

lessons.title: Throw and handle a specific error
lessons.explanation: A throwing function can return a value or report a failure. Declare an Error type for failures the caller can distinguish. Use try at the call site and choose how to respond in a do-catch block.

api.name: Error
api.description: Conform an enum or another type to represent failures.

api.name: throws
api.description: Declare that a function can throw.

api.name: do / catch
api.description: Handle errors from operations marked with try.

lessons.practice: Parse a percentage and distinguish malformed text from a number outside 0 through 100.
lessons.pitfall: Use an error case that matches the failed rule. Keep a broader catch after specific patterns when other errors are possible.

references.title: The Swift Programming Language: Error Handling

exercise.expected: Handle each failure with its own message and print valid percentages.
exercise.completion: The inputs "20", "101", and "twenty" exercise success, range failure, and conversion failure.
